reader.instructions: A finished, gated card is ready to be read for landing. Choose exactly one reader. The criteria below are the whole rule and docs/decide/criteria-reader.md is their long form, which the asker embeds in the state above this question; answer from the state's fields, never from the card's prose. The cost is not symmetric: a needless friend read costs a friend a few minutes, and a missed HOLD lands a defect on dev. When two readers are arguable, name the friend.

criteria.johnny: ANY of: the change execs a process, pushes, reads the environment or a secret, touches the sandbox, sudo, deploy keys or the network, or lands in the reaper, the launcher or the merge machinery. state field security_shaped_package=yes is this answer on its own, at any confidence. Measured 2026-09-19: both cards whose state said yes (#1815, #1871) were HELD by Johnny.
criteria.stella: ANY of: the card took a design default no ruling covers (state field design_defaults_taken is 1 or more), the spec is silent or contradictory on what was built, normative spec text moved, or the judgement is about kernel semantics or scope rather than code. Measured 2026-09-19: six pull requests were HELD by Stella and every one of them had taken a named design default or moved normative text; #1856 named FOUR and was still sent to opus-child, and Stella held it.
criteria.emma: Go correctness, tests, or documentation checked against what a binary prints, inside a lane Emma owns, where the design is already settled. state field friend_holds_the_area=emma is a strong pull to this answer.
criteria.opus-child: The default. A self-contained mechanical change inside ONE package, with a red test and a one-edit control, no spec question, no design default taken, and security_shaped_package=no. Measured 2026-09-19: 38 of 47 cards were this, and none of the 38 was later held.
criteria.fable-child: As opus-child, where a SECOND independent reading of the same small mechanical card is worth more than a first reading by the usual one.
criteria.rowan: Only where the open question is a coordination call -- landing order, sequencing, which of two branches goes first -- and not the code. Measured 2026-09-19: rowan was answered on 10 cards and not one of them turned out to be a coordination call.
